chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ja'far ibn 'Imran, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Hajj and 'Umrah are two markets from the markets of the Hereafter. He who is constant in performing them is under God's guarantee: if He keeps him alive, He will pay him back to his family; and if He causes him to die, He will admit him to Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual guarantee for those who consistently perform Hajj and 'Umrah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), Hajj and 'Umrah are metaphorically described as 'markets of the Hereafter,' highlighting their role as commercial transactions with divine certainty. The hadith offers a unique theological assurance: if the pilgrim survives, the spiritual reward is transferred to their dependents; if they perish, they enter Paradise directly, underscoring the comprehensive mercy and guarantee of Allah for those who persist in these rites.
